messages.content: You are BioGPT, an expert compiler architect. Translate the provided natural language biological protocol into valid, deterministic BioScript code for execution on a microfluidic biochip.

ASSAY TYPE: Multimodal Digital Microfluidic (Cellspot) Testing Platform for Antibody-Producing Cell Lines - Live/Dead Viability Assay and Fluorescent-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (FLISA) for Secreted IgG Quantification

REAGENTS USED:
  - Cell Sample (CHO DG44-Adalimumab cell suspension / culture supernatant containing secreted IgG)
  - Hoechst 33342 Stain (nuclear stain, labels total cell population)
  - Propidium Iodide (PI) Stain (labels non-viable/dead cells)
  - Protein A Magnetic Beads (Dynabeads Protein A, captures secreted IgG)
  - Wash Buffer
  - Fluorescent Secondary Antibody (Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated, labels captured IgG for FLISA readout)

STEPS:
1-2. Viability staining: Load the cell sample droplet, combine with Hoechst 33342 stain, and incubate to label all cells (total count channel).
3. Combine the Hoechst-stained droplet with propidium iodide stain and incubate at room temperature to label non-viable cells (dead count channel).
4. Detection: Image the stained droplet in the blue (Hoechst, total cells) and red (PI, dead cells) fluorescence channels; calculate cell viability (%) as Hoechst count / (Hoechst count + PI count) x 100. If the dead-cell signal is at or above threshold, the droplet is discarded.
5-6. FLISA bead capture: Load a fresh cell-culture-supernatant droplet containing secreted IgG, combine with a suspension of Protein A magnetic beads, and incubate to capture IgG onto the beads.
7. Magnetic bead wash: Pellet the beads using an adjacent magnetic plate and wash the bead pellet three times with wash buffer to remove unbound material.
8. Fluorescent labeling: Combine the washed bead pellet with fluorescent (Alexa Fluor 488) secondary antibody and incubate to label captured IgG.
9. Post-label wash: Pellet the beads magnetically and wash twice more with wash buffer to remove unbound secondary antibody.
10. Detection: Image the bead pellet by fluorescence microscopy; quantify integrated fluorescence intensity per bead area and convert to IgG concentration (ug/mL) using a Gompertz-model standard curve fit to a human IgG reference standard. If the fluorescence signal is below threshold, the sample is discarded.

INTERPRETATION: Successful platform validation is confirmed by reproducible dispensing/capture across replicate Cellspot electrode geometries (Fig. S1-S3), clear spectral separation of Hoechst (total) and PI (dead) signals with no cross-channel bleed-through (Fig. S4), efficient magnetic bead pelleting at optimized magnet distances (Fig. S5), IgG titer increasing over cultivation time consistent with orthogonal Octet BLI measurements and no significant difference between purified Adalimumab and generic human IgG standard calibration curves (Fig. S6), and accurate on-chip pH sensing via adhered optical patches (Fig. S7), supporting use of the Cellspot platform for semi-automated, multimodal monitoring of antibody-producing cell line health and productivity.

module fluorescence

manifest cell_sample
manifest hoechst_stain
manifest pi_stain
manifest protein_a_beads
manifest wash_buffer
manifest fluorescent_secondary_antibody

instructions:

// --- Viability assay: Hoechst (total cells) + Propidium Iodide (dead cells) ---
sample1 = dispense 10 units of cell_sample
hoechst = dispense 5 units of hoechst_stain
stained = mix sample1 with hoechst for 300s

pi = dispense 5 units of pi_stain
stained2 = mix stained with pi for 300s
heat stained2 at 25c for 5m

live_signal = detect fluorescence on stained2 for 10s
dead_signal = detect fluorescence on stained2 for 10s

if (dead_signal >= 50) {
    dispose stained2
}

heat stained2 at 25c for 1m
dispose stained2

// --- FLISA assay: Protein A bead capture of secreted IgG, fluorescent detection ---
sample2 = dispense 10 units of cell_sample
beads = dispense 10 units of protein_a_beads
capture = mix sample2 with beads for 600s
heat capture at 25c for 10m

repeat 3 times {
    wash = dispense 50 units of wash_buffer
    capture = mix capture with wash for 30s
}

secondary = dispense 10 units of fluorescent_secondary_antibody
labeled = mix capture with secondary for 300s
heat labeled at 25c for 15m

repeat 2 times {
    wash2 = dispense 50 units of wash_buffer
    labeled = mix labeled with wash2 for 30s
}

igg_signal = detect fluorescence on labeled for 10s

if (igg_signal < 50) {
    dispose labeled
}

heat labeled at 25c for 1m
dispose labeled

metadata.protocol_name: Semi-Automated Cell Line Optimization Protocol for Monoclonal Antibodies (Dixon et al., Lab Chip 2024)

sources.title: A multimodal digital microfluidic testing platform for antibody-producing cell lines

metadata.notes: The authored BioScript code models the two core fluorescence-based readouts of the Cellspot multimodal platform: (1) a Hoechst 33342 / propidium iodide (PI) live-dead viability assay, and (2) a Protein A bead-based FLISA immunoassay for secreted IgG. Because BioScript has no dedicated electrode-geometry, magnetic-bead-pelleting, or optical pH-sensor primitives, the electrode dispensing optimization (Figure S1), pH-sensor patch stretch/absorption steps (Figures S2 and S7), device/software implementation (Figure S3), and magnetic plate positioning used for bead pelleting (Figure S5) are abstracted into generic dispense/mix/wash operations; magnetic bead washing is modeled as a repeat-loop of fresh wash-buffer mixes analogous to the bead clean-up pattern used in other translated protocols. The viability assay models combined Hoechst+PI staining (as validated compatible in Figure S4) followed by two non-consuming 'detect fluorescence' calls representing the separate blue (total, Hoechst) and red (dead, PI) channel reads; the ratio-based percent-viability calculation itself is a post-hoc analysis step (Supplemental Methods) with no BioScript arithmetic primitive, so only the underlying fluorescence detection is captured, and the if-block threshold check stands in for a low-viability rejection call. The FLISA flow models Protein A bead capture of secreted IgG, a wash cycle, fluorescent secondary antibody labeling, a second wash cycle, and a final 'detect fluorescence' readout standing in for the Fiji/ImageJ bead fluorescence-per-area quantification and Gompertz-model IgG concentration conversion described in the Supplemental Methods; those downstream image-analysis and curve-fitting calculations have no BioScript primitive and are not modeled. The FLISA benchmarking against Sartorius Octet BLI (Figure S6) is an orthogonal validation experiment and is not modeled.

numeric_mismatches.note: The paper computes a continuous percent-viability ratio from Hoechst and PI particle counts via Fiji/ImageJ macro analysis rather than a fixed fluorescence-intensity cutoff; a threshold value was chosen for this translation since BioScript's if-condition requires a numeric comparison and has no ratio/formula primitive.

The paper converts observed bead fluorescence/area to an IgG concentration using a fitted Gompertz model (y = 4460.474*exp(-8.821*exp(-11.79x))), not a simple threshold; a placeholder threshold was used since BioScript has no curve-fitting or arithmetic-expression primitive.

numeric_mismatches.field: repeat 3 times / repeat 2 times wash loops
numeric_mismatches.note: The paper describes magnetic bead pelleting and washing qualitatively (Figure S5) without a stated fixed wash-cycle count; three and two wash cycles were chosen as reasonable discretizations for this translation, not values stated verbatim in the SI text.

numeric_mismatches.field: Cellspot electrode dispensing optimization (Fig. S1), pH sensor patch stretching (Figs. S2, S7), device/software implementation (Fig. S3), magnetic plate optimization (Fig. S5), Octet BLI benchmarking (Fig. S6)
numeric_mismatches.note: Not modeled. These are hardware/electrode-design optimization, device-software, optical pH-sensing, and orthogonal instrument-benchmarking sub-experiments with no corresponding BioScript primitive, and fall outside the scope of this translation; only the core viability and FLISA fluorescence assay chemistry is captured here.
